approachQuestion.prompt:
Archived Batch Merge

The mutable array archive has length p+q. Its first p entries are sorted integer timestamps; its last q cells are unused writable capacity whose values must be ignored. A read-only array incoming has q timestamps sorted in nondecreasing order. Put the sorted multiset union of the p valid archive entries and incoming into archive. Preserve duplicates, and return archive itself. incoming does not share storage with archive.

Constraints: 0 <= p,q <= 200000; timestamps are in [-1000000000,1000000000]. Neither array may be resized.

Example 1: p=3, archive=[1,4,4,0,0], incoming=[2,4] -> [1,2,4,4,4].
Example 2: p=0, archive=[0,0], incoming=[-2,3] -> [-2,3].
Example 3: p=2, archive=[1,2], incoming=[] -> [1,2].
constraints: Choose the most efficient valid approach for the entire stated input domain; accept equivalent optimal variants.

options.text: Read the valid archive prefix and incoming from their ends. Write the larger remaining entry into the last unfilled archive cell and consume its source; after either source empties, finish the other source from the back.
options.feedback: The write position stays at or beyond every unread archive position; incoming is separate. Repeated values are consumed one at a time.

options.text: Copy the p valid archive entries, then merge that copy and incoming forward into archive.
options.feedback: The copied prefix prevents overwrite and gives the right answer, but using the unused capacity from the back removes that copy.

options.text: Merge forward directly from archive[0] and incoming[0], writing each chosen entry into the next archive cell without copying or shifting unread entries.
options.feedback: For p=1, archive=[3,0], incoming=[1], writing 1 at archive[0] destroys the unread 3.

options.text: Copy incoming into the unused cells and return archive.
options.feedback: For p=1, archive=[3,0], incoming=[1], this returns [3,1], which is unsorted.

feedback.reason: Merge into supplied spare capacity from the safe direction so output writes cannot overwrite unread input.
details: Initialize source indices p-1 and q-1 and an output index p+q-1. Repeatedly write the larger available source value into the output cell and decrease the corresponding source index. When either source is exhausted, write the remaining source backward into the remaining cells, including self-writes from archive.

Writing from the end protects archive values that have not yet been merged. Supplied spare capacity belongs to the input/output allocation, not a new helper array. The fixed method includes its specified remaining self-writes.

Write the larger remaining entry into the last unfilled archive cell and consume its source; after either source empties, finish the other source from the back.”: The write position stays at or beyond every unread archive position; incoming is separate. Repeated values are consumed one at a time.

“Copy the p valid archive entries, then merge that copy and incoming forward into archive.”: The copied prefix prevents overwrite and gives the right answer, but using the unused capacity from the back removes that copy.

“Merge forward directly from archive[0] and incoming[0], writing each chosen entry into the next archive cell without copying or shifting unread entries.”: For p=1, archive=[3,0], incoming=[1], writing 1 at archive[0] destroys the unread 3.
“Copy incoming into the unused cells and return archive.”: For p=1, archive=[3,0], incoming=[1], this returns [3,1], which is unsorted.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed after question 1, choose its tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed access and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include all temporary buffers, input copies, and call frames; exclude supplied input and returned output. p and q are the valid source lengths. The output is the same supplied archive array. All merges are iterative, without resizing, copies, recursion, hashing, or amortized container operations.
constraints: Analyze this fixed method regardless of your answer to question 1; choose the tightest pair.

options.text: O(p + q + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(p + q + 1) time, O(p + q + 1) auxiliary space
O((p + q + 1) log(p + q + 2)) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Backward merging writes all p+q output cells with fixed indices.
details: This specified method writes all p+q output cells, including self-writes if incoming is empty. Each source index moves only backward. The worst-case time is O(p+q+1) and auxiliary storage is a few indices and one value; the supplied writable capacity is input/output storage.

Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed access and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include all temporary buffers, input copies, and call frames; exclude supplied input and returned output. p and q are the valid source lengths. The output is the same supplied archive array. All merges are iterative, without resizing, copies, recursion, hashing, or amortized container operations.
“O(p + q + 1) time, O(p + q + 1) auxiliary space”: This adds temporary source storage that the backward merge avoids.
“O((p + 1)(q + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: No shifting or restarted search is performed.
“O((p + q + 1) log(p + q + 2)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This is a general sorting cost, not the specified merge.
